description: Structural roadmap and future evolution goals of the susi substrate (agent governance — not end-user docs).
title: SUSI Substrate Roadmap: The Sovereign Will

vectors.progress: PARTIAL: UDP LAN discovery, TCP JSON-RPC peer dispatch, and trust-score ranking already worked. Closed the routing gap the code itself flagged ("bloom-filters of peer registries for perfect routing"): peers now exchange a real 256-bit `CapabilityBloom` of their registered tool names during ping/pong, and `rank_peers_for_goal` scores peers by goal/capability overlap instead of trust alone (`src/gawd/amas.rs`). As of 2026-09-22 (EV-2022922-101), added a real quorum-commit primitive: `SusiSupervisor::quorum_majority` (`src/gawd/amas.rs`) checks the shared mission blackboard — which already holds both local agent outputs and dispatched peer-node outputs under `PeerNode_<id>` keys — for a strict majority of independently-produced entries that exact-match after normalization, and commits that value directly (a new `QUORUM_COMMIT` A2A action, distinct from the pre-existing `STATE_CONVERGENCE` rank-leader/LLM-synthesis paths) instead of only ever picking one rank-leader's answer or asking an LLM to reconcile. Remaining gap narrowed (cluster-key membership landed): peers now exchange an HMAC-SHA256-signed ping/pong (`SUSI_PING_SIG`/`SUSI_PONG_SIG`, susi-peer-v1) keyed by a shared 32-byte secret at ~/.susi/cluster.key (0600, `susi_config::cluster_key`); a pong must echo the requester's nonce, so a spoofed or replayed UDP answer can never promote a peer past `PeerAdmission::Discovered`. Verified peers persist in ~/.susi/peers.json and rehydrate as `Explicit` on restart. As of 2026-09-23, the quorum vote tolerates mid-vote churn via a pinned electorate (the Raft configuration-entry concept applied to one consensus round): supervise_mission snapshots the voter set at broadcast — local fleet names + PeerNode_<id> keys for every Explicit peer actually dispatched — and quorum_majority counts only pinned members, thresholding against the electorate's full size rather than the respondents. A peer dying mid-vote now shrinks the response set instead of silently lowering the quorum bar, and a peer admitted after the broadcast can never tilt the count. Commit replication landed (kernel-ABI commit_log module, vendored to all planes): every QUORUM_COMMIT is sealed into a CommitRecord (pinned electorate, tally, quorum threshold, SHA-256 value hash, HMAC-SHA256 signature under cluster.key), appended to ~/.susi/commit_log.jsonl, and pushed to each voting peer via the governed commit_record tool — receivers verify signature + quorum consistency before appending, so forged or below-quorum records fail closed. A coordinator crash mid-round no longer loses the decision, and commit_log exposes the ledger for audit. Still missing vs Raft/Paxos: no leader election and no term/index ordering — records are signed decisions, not a replicated state-machine log, so a peer cannot reconstruct cluster state from its ledger alone.

PARTIAL, reinterpreted: literal runtime Rust trait patching isn't achievable in safe Rust. Delivered the real equivalent — `resolve_capability_gap` now falls back to `ReflexSynthesizer::synthesize_wasm_reflex`, which generates and compiles an input-dependent WASI reflex and hot-loads it via the existing `reflex_<name>` convention with **no daemon restart** (`src/gawd/reflex_synth.rs`, `src/gmcp/tools/mod.rs`). Also fixed two latent bugs found while building this: the target triple (`wasm32-wasi`, removed from rustc) was corrected to `wasm32-wasip1`, and the synthesized source previously had no `fn main()`/`_start`, so it could never have executed even if it had compiled. Compilation requires the `wasm32-wasip1` rustup target; the live end-to-end test (`test_wasm_reflex_hot_patch_end_to_end`) honestly skips (not silently) when that target is absent rather than assuming success. As of 2026-09-22 (EV-2022922-099), that target IS installed in this dev environment and the test was run directly (not just checked for the skip path): it took the real compile-and-execute branch and passed, `rustc --target wasm32-wasip1` compiling the synthesized reflex and `WasmHost::execute_reflex` running it under WASI with correct output. This confirms the full live path genuinely works, at least in one environment with the toolchain present — it is still environment-dependent (unverified whether `wasm32-wasip1` is installed in CI or other dev machines), and this run only exercised `synthesize_wasm_reflex` + `WasmHost::execute_reflex` directly, not a full pass through `resolve_capability_gap`'s own call site.
